example.title: ISO 5167-2 orifice metering run
example.source: ISO 5167-2:2003, Measurement of fluid flow by means of pressure differential devices -- Part 2: Orifice plates. Eq. (4) (Reader-Harris/Gallagher C), the flow equation, and 5.4.1 (pressure loss).
example.reproduced: A metering run: air at 300 K in a 100 mm pipe, a square-edged plate of beta = 0.5 with flange taps, and a pipe downstream, between 2 bar and 1.95 bar. The plate drives from the approach pipe's static pressure with the velocity-of-approach factor E, and between pipes it charges only the permanent loss of 5.4.1 to the system.
example.where_to_look: Solve, then select the orifice plate. dP_tap is the flange-tap differential a meter would read (about 6.5 kPa); dP_permanent is what the plate costs the system (about 4.8 kPa, 73% of it, as 5.4.1 gives at beta 0.5). Cd is the Reader-Harris/Gallagher C at D and D/2 taps, beta and E the velocity-of-approach terms.
example.label: fidelity
example.label_note: Checked against the standard's own equations, not against measurements: C to 3e-6, the permanent loss to 1e-4. Reading dP_tap back through ISO's flow equation returns the solved flow to 0.9% (exactly when the network runs incompressible): the compressible orifice kernel against ISO's empirical expansibility.
